s1.syndrome_frame: Intermittent neurological symptoms with associated gastrointestinal symptoms and imaging findings suggestive of a posterior fossa lesion
salient_findings: Intermittent dizziness and blurred vision
Nausea and vomiting that improve after vomiting
Posterior occipital tingling that worsens with emotional agitation
Irregular high-density mass shadow in posterior fossa on CT scan
Irregular mixed signals in medial and posterior cerebellum on MRI
key_facts: 18-year history of intermittent dizziness and blurred vision
Symptoms accompanied by nausea and vomiting
Symptoms improve after vomiting
Posterior occipital tingling worsens with emotional agitation
Symptoms became more frequent by September 2021
CT scan shows irregular high-density mass shadow in posterior fossa
CT value approximately 93HU
MRI shows irregular mixed signals in medial and posterior cerebellum
Maximum size of lesion: 50mm × 41mm × 51mm
Line-like septum and complex nodules present on MRI
Cerebrospinal fluid: AFP and β-HCG negative
Cyst fluid analysis shows total protein, albumin, globulin, total cholesterol, and triglyceride

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior fossa location and imaging characteristics match

shortlist.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common in young adults and can present with similar symptoms

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can occur in posterior fossa and present with neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Arachnoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging findings could be consistent with a cystic lesion

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Can occur in posterior fossa and present with neurological symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of a cystic lesion with a mural nodule in the posterior fossa, as shown on MRI, along with the patient's symptoms and the cyst fluid analysis, is most consistent with hemangioblastoma. The high-density mass shadow on CT and the mixed signals on MRI also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pilocytic astrocytoma
rejected.why: While pilocytic astrocytoma can present with a cystic component and a mural nodule, the location and imaging characteristics are less typical for this diagnosis compared to hemangioblastoma.

rejected.label: Ependymoma
rejected.why: Ependymomas are more commonly associated with the ventricular system and spinal cord, and the imaging findings do not strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Arachnoid cyst
rejected.why: Arachnoid cysts typically appear as homogeneous, low-density lesions on CT and do not contain nodules or septa, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningiomas are usually dural-based and have a different appearance on imaging, with more homogeneous enhancement and a broader dural attachment, which is not described in this case.
